newsitem.title: USA: Colorado couple's wedding disrupted by G-7.
newsitem.headline: Colorado couple's wedding disrupted by G-7.

text.p: Brad Irwin and Suzanne Terry thought they had found the perfect site for their dream wedding reception -- a beautiful museum with a panoramic view of the Rocky Mountains.

But their dream turned to tears when they discovered they had been bumped by the G-7 summit of industrialised nations, which plans to use the Denver Museum of Natural History during its June 20-22 meetings.
The couple had already paid a $1,000 deposit to the museum for their June 21 reception and Irwin said it was too late to find another place during the popular June wedding season.

The White House said it had no idea the couple had rented the museum when the site was chosen for the meetings. "We were assured that there were no conflicts with the Denver summit before we ever considered the museum as a meeting site," an administration official said.

White House spokeswoman Mary Ellen Glynn said on Friday she was optimistic the conflict would be resolved. "The mayor's office and folks from the Denver summit are working with the couple to find an acceptable solution to what will certainly be the happiest day of their lives," Glynn said.
Irwin, an attorney, said he did not want to put his fiancee through a lawsuit and trial over the site. "She's been crying for six or seven days," he said.
